newsitem.title: USA: Dow Industrials down at midday.
newsitem.headline: Dow Industrials down at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were down at midday Thursday on weak bonds, mixed techs and a carryover of profit-taking from yesterday's Dow decline.
Analysts said there were signs the dollar had topped out in the short-term, and this could end the stampede of foreign money into U.S. markets.
Cautious comments by Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Cohen gave investors a bit of additional incentive to take profits, but market watchers said this would have happened anyway.
The Dow was down 43 points at 6977.

Big Board declines led advancing issues by 13 to 10 on volume of about 236 million shares. The Nasdaq Composite Index was down 10 points at 1356, reflecting a mixed tech sector and the weight of a sell-off in shares of Intel Corp.

"We are following up on the late weakness yesterday. The major indices are in the stratosphere, techs continue to trade in a volatile fashion, with market leadership stocks coming in for some profit-taking," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"Near-term, we're in for a little tough sledding."

"It's a tired blue chip market. Did people really expect the market to make it to year's end without some profit-taking? You saw it yesterday and you see it today in the blue chips," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "The pause was going to come sooner or later. Even the bond market has gotten ahead of itself."
U.S. Treasuries were lower, with the long bond down 13/32 to yield 6.61 percent.
Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said that there was evidence that the dollar had topped out in the near-term.
"If this proves to be true, you will see an end to the desperate stampede of foreign money into American financial instruments," Metz said.
In afternoon European trading, the dollar edged back above 123 yen.
Metz said that the bond market also appeared to have run out steam, highlighting the overvaluation of the stock market.
"The earnings outlook is still good, but it is mixed in some sectors. Some high tech companies are saying that growth will be there this year, but that expectations are too optimistic."

Analysts said that investors may be using Cohen's comments as a pretext for taking profits. Cohen adjusted her bullish view and said that the stock market could be heading for a trading range. The comments were made last Friday in a fax to clients but became the focus of interest again after the Wall Street Journal featured them in today's edition.
"Her comments certainly aren't helping the market today," Metz said. But Prime Charter's Bleier said that there was nothing new in what the Journal reported today.
"This is not new news. This is only new for the newspapers, not for the market," Bleier said.

Intel Corp, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, fell 2-1/2 to 151-3/8 while direct competitor Cyrix Corp was up 4-3/8 at 29-7/8 on positive expectations for the company's new computer chip designed for use in reduced-cost personal computers.
